implementation_notes: Rust has no stable prefetch intrinsic in std; the intrinsic is _mm_prefetch (x86) or the inline asm equivalent, reached via the core::arch intrinsics or the prefetch crate. For the common case - a pointer chase through an owned structure - the idiomatic answer is layout (a Vec of a contiguous struct, or indices into a flat arena, is the prefetchable form) rather than a hint. Unsafe Rust makes the manual prefetch possible (you know the address is valid because you hold the reference), but the win must be measured. For files, madvise(MADV_WILLNEED) via libc and posix_fadvise are available through the libc crate. The real Rust lever for a chase is the arena pattern - store all nodes in one Vec and traverse by index, so the indices are sequential even though the graph is random.
idiom_name: core::arch _mm_prefetch / the prefetch crate for CPU hints; madvise(MADV_WILLNEED) via libc for pages
pitfalls: No stable prefetch in std; _mm_prefetch is x86-specific and needs unsafe (you must guarantee the address is valid).
The prefetch crate wraps the intrinsic, but the win must be measured - the arena-by-index layout usually beats a hint.
For a pointer chase the idiomatic Rust fix is an arena (one Vec, traverse by index), which makes the memory access sequential without any hint.
madvise via the libc crate is advice and can fail (ENOMEM); it is not a guarantee the pages are resident.
